cosy-lesson.title: "People don't fake depression, they fake being okay.": Robin Williams

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Facade – an outward appearance that conceals a less pleasant reality.

p.em: Example: She maintained a cheerful facade despite her personal troubles.

cosy-blockquote.p: Stigma – a mark of disgrace associated with a particular circumstance.

p.em: Example: We must work to reduce the social stigma of mental illness.

cosy-blockquote.p: Fake – to pretend to feel or have something.

p.em: Example: It is hard to fake happiness when you feel sad.

cosy-blockquote.p: Conceal – to keep something secret or prevent it from being known.

p.em: Example: He tried to conceal his anxiety with a wide smile.

cosy-blockquote.p: Depressed – suffering from severe despondency and dejection.

p.em: Example: He felt depressed after losing his job but sought help.

cosy-blockquote.p: Empathy – the ability to understand other's feelings.

p.em: Example: Hearing people's thoughts taught him true empathy, replacing his cold apathy.

cosy-blockquote.p: Struggle – to strive to achieve or attain something in the face of difficulties.

p.em: Example: Many people struggle in silence before asking for help.

cosy-blockquote.p: Authentic – of undisputed origin; genuine and true.

p.em: Example: Sharing your true feelings is a sign of an authentic connection.

cosy-blockquote.p: Mask – to cover or hide a feeling or reality.

p.em: Example: She tried to mask her disappointment when she heard the news.

cosy-blockquote.p: Vulnerability – state of being exposed to the possibility of being attacked or harmed.

p.em: Example: Embracing vulnerability is a far more courageous path than pretending to possess absolute strength.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
Why do people build a smiling facade when they are hurting inside?
★ Have you ever used a happy facade to hide a bad day?

How does social stigma prevent people from admitting they need emotional help?
★ Have you ever felt that talking about your feelings carried a social stigma?

Why do we feel pressured to fake being happy when we are around other people?
★ Is it easy for you to spot when someone is trying to fake their laughter?

What makes us want to conceal our deepest sadness even from close friends?
★ Do you usually conceal your worries, or do you prefer to talk about them?

What is the difference between feeling temporarily sad and being clinically depressed?
★ Have you ever supported a friend who was feeling severely depressed?

How can showing true empathy help someone who feels completely alone?
★ Who in your life shows you the most empathy when you are upset?

Why do many individuals struggle in silence rather than ask for help?
★ What is your healthiest habit when you have to face a personal struggle?

How does having an authentic conversation with someone change our mood?
★ Do you feel you can be fully authentic when talking to your family?

Why is it exhausting to constantly mask our true feelings at work or school?
★ At what times of the day do you feel you can finally take off your emotional mask?

Why is showing our vulnerability a sign of courage rather than weakness?
★ Is it difficult for you to show your vulnerability in front of others?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: collaborative task or visual analysis in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, work together on the following task:

cosy-blockquote.p: Discuss with your partner: How do we support someone who is faking being okay? Rank these supportive methods from most to least helpful: - 🔇 Active Listening Just sitting in silence and listening without giving any unsolicited advice or solutions. - 🤍 Validating Feelings Saying "It is okay not to be okay right now," accepting their sadness exactly as it is. - 🍵 Gentle Presence Offering a simple cup of tea or a walk, without demanding any deep or heavy conversations. - 🔓 Honest Sharing Showing your own vulnerability first, so they feel safe to take off their emotional mask.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: 1-on-1 guided visual description and task response with teacher.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
In the future, social expectations will change so much that wearing a smiling facade will no longer be necessary. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you be happier if society allowed everyone to stop pretending to be okay?

Future schools will teach emotional intelligence, completely removing the stigma of mental health. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ If you were a teacher, would you prioritize mental health over academic grades?

Advanced AI companions will be programmed so they never fake happiness, helping us learn to be more honest. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you feel comfortable sharing your worries with a perfectly honest AI robot?

Modern life will become so transparent that people will no longer be able to conceal their true emotions. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ If technology could read your feelings, would you want it to be turned off?

A future world with less work and more free time will ensure that nobody ever feels depressed or isolated. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ If you had unlimited free time, how would you protect your mental health?

Future communication technology will allow us to share and feel each other's emotions, creating perfect empathy. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you wear a device if it could transfer your emotions to a loved one?

In the coming decades, society will recognize that to struggle with sadness is a natural part of being human. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would life be better if we were always happy, without any emotional challenges?

Future social networks will reward authentic self-expression instead of idealized profiles. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ If social media did not exist, would you feel more connected to your true self?

Future employers will ban the pressure to smile, allowing workers to never mask their professional stress. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ If your boss offered mental health days, would you feel more relaxed at work?

A future society that embraces vulnerability will have far fewer mental health crises than today. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ If we stopped pretending to be okay, would our friendships become stronger?

ul.li: Incorrect: I am depress today → Correct: I feel depressed today ((Use participle adjective 'depressed'))
Incorrect: He fakes to be happy → Correct: He fakes being happy ((Fake + gerund))
Incorrect: It depend on person → Correct: It depends on the person ((Depends on + article))
